### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/view.md`, `packages/spec/liveness/view.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via retiredAfter (symbol, a field of const object viewListFilterableFieldsRemoved), retiredFromLoadPath (symbol, a field of const object viewListFilterableFieldsRemoved))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/view.md`, `packages/spec/liveness/view.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **143** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 54159fd742e5a79fc10ac41854dba3395e1a1ffe` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `770c2759b7f3cff12e3718703e084d83527d3eff` — the merge of head `bb71914fc92a679303b28361f1cd9384bb9baa30` into base `54159fd742e5a79fc10ac41854dba3395e1a1ffe`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 770c2759b7f3cff12e3718703e084d83527d3eff && git checkout 770c2759b7f3cff12e3718703e084d83527d3eff
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 54159fd742e5a79fc10ac41854dba3395e1a1ffe bb71914fc92a679303b28361f1cd9384bb9baa30 && git checkout -B drift-repro 54159fd742e5a79fc10ac41854dba3395e1a1ffe && git merge --no-ff bb71914fc92a679303b28361f1cd9384bb9baa30

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 54159fd742e5a79fc10ac41854dba3395e1a1ffe
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 54159fd742e5a79fc10ac41854dba3395e1a1ffe` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

**D1 — ruling C and no wider: RIGHT.** The diff removes exactly one authorable key, `filterableFields`, from one shape, `ListViewShapeSchema` (`view.zod.ts`), by `retiredKey(LIST_VIEW_FILTERABLE_FIELDS_RETIRED)`. Every list-view door derives from that shape by reference, read at head: `ListViewSchema`; `ObjectListViewSchema` is `ListViewShapeSchema.omit({ userFilters }).extend(...)`; the runtime write door's list overlay arm (`ListViewOverlayWireSchema`) is `ListViewShapeSchema.extend(...)`; a page `list-view` node's `ListViewPageProps` spreads `ListViewSchema.shape`. So the tombstone is refused at every door the pin names, eight in all, and `getMetadataTypeSchema('view')` is pinned to `ViewMetadataSchema`. No replacement key is added anywhere in the diff. `searchableFields` and `userFilters` are not touched in `view.zod.ts`; the diff's only other `view.zod.ts` change is the prescription constant and the docblock. The Studio form row leaves (`view.form.ts`) and `userFilters` stays under End-user controls (`view.form.ts:170-175`).

**D2 — the prescription is true: RIGHT.** It names `userFilters` with the `dropdown` element and a `fields` array of `{ field }` entries, which is the `UserFiltersSchema` shape, and says the Filter panel offers every field the user may read, field read security deciding, a field the object marks `hidden: true` not offered. Checked against objectui `origin/main` `packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx:4654-4680`, the `filterFields` memo: with no whitelist the candidate list is `candidateFields` filtered by `canReadField(perms, objectName, field)` and then by `!isHidden(field) || held.has(field)`. That is every readable field minus `hidden` ones, with one edge the prescription does not mention and does not need to: a hidden field already held by a saved condition stays offered. The closing `os migrate meta --from 17` sentence is the standardized one (`retired-key.ts`). No tracker number in the prescription, pinned.

**D3 — a DROP, never a rewrite: RIGHT.** `view-list-filterable-fields-removed` applies `mapViewPayloads` over the stack and, for a payload whose kind is `list`, returns `stripKeys(payload, ['filterableFields'], emit, path)`, every other payload untouched: byte-for-byte the shape of the 17.x `view-list-passthrough-keys-removed` and the 18.x `view-list-tabs-removed`. `stripKeys` emits `to: '(removed)'` and deletes; nothing writes `userFilters`. Pinned: notices read `(removed)`, no `userFilters` is minted where none was written, an authored one rides through unchanged, and a second replay converts nothing.

**D4 — the conversion metadata is right by the registry's own rules: RIGHT.** `toMajor: 18` matches `PROTOCOL_VERSION` major 18 (Check Changeset's lockstep line). `retiredFromLoadPath: true` is the pair of the tombstone, as `RetiredConversionState` in `types.ts` describes: the authoring funnel no longer replays it, so a live author meets the tombstone, while `applyConversionsToStoredItem` pins `includeRetired: true` and strips a stored row. `retiredAfter: '17.7.0'` follows the rule on that field: under a prerelease label (`@objectstack/spec` is `18.0.0-next.5` at head) it is the newest published stable, never the label. The census's last release is `17.4.0`, so `retired-after.census.test.ts` admits the half-open range from `17.4.0` up to but excluding `18.0.0`; `17.7.0` is inside it; the Check Changeset job's own fetch lists `@objectstack/spec@17.7.0` as the newest stable spec tag before the `18.0.0-next` series; and 17 other step-18 entries at head carry the same stamp. The entry is inserted in `MAJOR_18_CONVERSIONS` in id order with `order: 71`, unique in that table; the rationale fragment's `order: 105` is unique in `STEP18_RATIONALE`.

**D5 — the D3 entry and the retired-keys entries are true: RIGHT.** `18.list-view-filterable-fields-retired.ts` names the surface, says nothing replaces the whitelist, names `userFilters` as the curated bar, states the stored-whitelist consequence honestly (the panel widens; a hidden field the whitelist named is no longer offered) and names the object-`listViews` boundary. The two retired-keys files follow `entries/README.md` exactly: filename derived from the id, the `//` run above `export const entry`, one per walked def, as the `17.ui__ListView__bordered` / `17.ui__ObjectListView__bordered` pair does. `check-adr-0087-registration` requires `registered` ids to resolve at head and be new in this diff; both are.

**D6 — the coverage boundary is honest and acceptable, with one stated cost: RIGHT.** `mapViewPayloads` (`walk.ts`) walks `stack.views[]` in its three spellings and nothing else. A grep of the head registry finds no conversion that reaches `objects[].listViews.*`; `applyConversionsToStoredItem('object', row)` therefore returns the row with the key still on it and `ObjectSchema` refuses it, which the pin's BOUNDARY test asserts. That does leave a stored object row carrying the key un-resavable without a hand edit. It is stated in the three places an operator reads: the changeset's stored-row paragraph (ships as `CHANGELOG.md`), the D3 entry's `reason` (the upgrade-guide projection) and the conversion docblock. The same boundary is carried by `view-list-tabs-removed` and the other list-view conversions, the object Studio form offers no `listViews` input at all (`object.form.ts`), and the in-tree population is zero. Accepted on that precedent; not a rider this PR could close without a new object-collection walker, which is its own card.

**D7 — generated artefacts are regenerated and consistent: RIGHT.** `authorable-surface/ui.json`: the two rows become `[RETIRED]`, the `bordered` precedent's spelling. `authorable-surface.base.json` is untouched, which is correct: `build-schemas.ts` says the anchor is rewritten only by `--update-base`, by hand, and the deletion gate reconciles a `[RETIRED]` shard row against the anchor through `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR`; `Lint & Repo Gates` is green. `liveness/view.json`: the row flips `live` to `dead` with `verifiedAt` and `evidenceScope: cross-repo`, and its note names the reader truthfully against objectui `origin/main` (the `filterFields` memo, fed by `app-shell` `ObjectView.tsx` and `plugin-view` `ObjectView.tsx`, withheld on a page node by `plugin-list/src/index.tsx`). Counting statuses in `view.json` at base and head gives live 72 to 71, dead 11 to 12; `state-counts/view.md` reads 79 to 78 and 11 to 12 because it sums the type's shards, so the deltas agree. The three reference pages carry ten rows that are each the prescription string verbatim, the generator's output. The four `metadata-forms` bundles each lose the same four-line `filterableFields` block and nothing else, which is what `check-i18n-bundles.mjs --write` produces when a source input leaves.

**D8 — the pins hold the change: RIGHT.** Per door: the refusal with issue code `invalid_type`, the path naming the key, the prescription, and the key-first convention; a control without the key; a boundary with `userFilters` and `searchableFields`. Plus the empty-array refusal, the registry binding, the prescription's content and its tracker-number absence, the tsc channel (`@ts-expect-error` under the test-layer typecheck, with the parse throwing the same prescription), the form walk with anti-vacuity neighbours, the stored-seam replay with notice ids and paths, the never-a-rewrite pin, the three-spelling reach plus idempotence, the retired-from-load-path pin, the object-`listViews` boundary, both `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR[18]` ids, the conversion id in the step-18 chain, the D3 entry's presence and content, a tree-scoped absence walk with a declared radius and a matcher battery, and the JOIN row for both defs in `retired-key-removal-version.pin.test.ts`. The dev's ablation count is consistent with that control flow: restoring the plain declaration fails the 8 door refusals, the empty-array refusal, the prescription-content pin, the tsc-channel parse, the object-`listViews` boundary (the object now parses) and the JOIN row, 13 in all, while the controls, boundaries, form walk, D2 pins (independent of the shape), registration pins and the tree walk hold.

**D9 — the RESIDUE assertion is right, with its cost named.** The assertion is the last loop of the test `no list-view payload carrying filterableFields survives inside the declared radius`: `expect(residueHits.get(rel) ?? 0, rel + ' no longer spells the key — delete its RESIDUE entry').toBeGreaterThan(0)`, over the four RESIDUE paths. It ratchets the right way. A RESIDUE entry skips the offender check for that file; without the greater-than-zero guard an entry would outlive its residue and silently exempt a future re-authoring there, which is exactly the allowlist the pin's own comment refuses. The red it produces on cleanup is the instruction to delete the entry in the same PR, and the message says so. It does not block the cleanup; it couples it: a `packages/lint`, `metadata-core` or `objectql` cleanup must also edit `packages/spec/src/ui/view-list-filterable-fields-retirement.test.ts`, one extra file, which `check:cross-package-test-inputs` already declares for this test. This is the `view-list-tabs-retirement.test.ts` shape verbatim (its RESIDUE set and the same assertion at its line 560). One difference worth knowing: the tabs pin's matcher requires a list-view sibling key beside `tabs`, while this pin counts any object literal whose own keys include `filterableFields`, which is why a lint severity map and a scrub vocabulary map count as offenders here. Looser, and loud rather than silent; acceptable.

**D10 — changeset body: RIGHT.** `BREAKING` banner, the FROM to TO table with both meanings the key carried, the one-line fix, a before/after block, the stored-row paragraph including the object-row sentence, the untouched-keys sentence, the not-measured out-of-repo note, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, and the ADR-0087 marker `registered` naming both new ids.

**D11 — out-of-lane paths: RIGHT and minimal.** `packages/platform-objects/**`: four generator outputs, and `object-lifecycle-panel-echo-decisions.test.ts` moves its positive-control count 674 to 673 with a provenance comment in the style of the prior entries; the removed input's label was authored in all three locales, so the catalog loses exactly one, which the four bundle diffs show. `content/docs/**`: three generated pages, and `architecture.mdx` replaces the retired key in a `defineView` list example with `userFilters: { element: 'dropdown', fields: [{ field: 'industry' }] }` and one comment line. That is a legal `ListViewSchema.userFilters` value, the example remains a list view, and the dropped `annual_revenue` entry was a number field that a dropdown quick filter would not suit. True against the spec.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` `minor` with `BREAKING` is what this diff publishes under the repository's rule: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is BREAKING and takes at least `minor`, and the 18 prerelease train admits no `major` bump (Check Changeset: "This diff introduces no major bump"; "LEVEL AXIS: this PR declares clause-② yes (narrowing), and no package whose published source it moves is graded patch"). `check:api-surface` reads unchanged because no export moves; the narrowing is at the key level and is carried by the tombstone's `never` input type, the parse refusal and the `[RETIRED]` rows. The `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` line is on both carriers, the PR body and the changeset. The `.changeset/pre.json` reading is literal: the file is `{ "mode": "exit", "tag": "next" }` and nothing else; the spec label is `18.0.0-next.5`; a `minor` increment of that prerelease under exit mode is `18.0.0`, so the sentence "the next version pass publishes this in 18.0.0" is true. The ADR-0087 registration is `registered view-list-filterable-fields-removed, list-view-filterable-fields-retired`, both ids new in this diff and resolving at head; `check-adr-0087-registration` is green inside Check Changeset.

### ③ Boundary flags

**F1 — the dev's deviations (a) to (f): accepted.** (a) The JOIN row, the rationale fragment, the `vitest.repo-tests.json` line and the two extra reference pages are each demanded by a gate or a generator on this surface. (b) The platform-objects count edit is declared above as D11 and accepted at this tier; it is the one out-of-lane hand edit. (c) and (d) are run-shape notes; the merge brought no new mention of the key, confirmed by the head-wide census (31 files mention it, every one accounted for by the diff, the residue, release-owned CHANGELOGs or the tabs pin's vocabulary list). (e) Seven build and publish tooling tests are not measured locally and belong to `Test Core`, which is in progress at this read. (f) Reported, not a deviation.

**F2 — ADR-0047 Decision 1 is falsified by this PR; a governed follow-up, not a blocker.** Confirmed at `docs/adr/0047-object-ui-run-modes.md:154-155`: "`filterableFields` stays as the legacy shorthand; loaders auto-upgrade it to `userFilters.fields` entries." After this PR the key does not stay and the ruling forbids the auto-upgrade, which was never built. The ADR's own section 4 Non-goals (`:253-254`) already calls that alias a "one-release courtesy, not a commitment", and the maintainer's verbatim 「C」 (record 6278975049) is the superseding word. Prime Directive 13 wants the record amended, and `docs/adr/**` is Tier H, so the amendment is a docs-only PR of its own, the dev's option A; folding it here would make this PR Tier H for a one-line status note. The seat files it when this lands. ADR-0047 is untouched by the diff.

**F3 — finding (1), the in-repo readers: reachable on one path, not dead; no duplicate beside the tombstone; follow-up.** `os validate` exits 1 at the `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema` parse before any rule runs, so the tombstone is the only finding there. `os lint` never Zod-parses (`lint.ts`: a schema error is `os validate`'s verdict) and runs the reference-integrity suite over `normalizeStackInput` output, which replays only live conversions, so a raw `filterableFields` survives to `validate-list-view-field-refs.ts` (`:392` severity `error`, `:534` role `filter`) and `validate-field-consumers.ts:307`. On that path a valid name produces no finding, so a retired key passes `os lint` silently, and a stale name produces a field-reference `error` that names the field rather than the retirement: a misleading finding only in that case, and a class that predates this PR for every tombstoned key, since `os lint` raises no tombstone at all. `metadata-diagnostics.ts:237` reads the key off a served view, but the served row has been through `applyConversionsToStoredItem` (`protocol.ts:6783`), which strips it, so that read is dead for `stack.views[]` spellings; the `tabs` retirement removed its own walk there and left a comment at `:231-235`, and this PR leaves the sibling walk in place. `rule-explanations.ts:3114` and `:3149` still name the key as a checked position in `os explain` text. `object-schema-fls-references.ts:719` keeps it in the ADR-0106 scrub vocabulary. None of these is an author, none is reached by a parsed stack, and the pin's RESIDUE set tracks the four that spell it as a key. Follow-up: delete the spellings, the metadata-diagnostics walk and the react-props mention together, and let the RESIDUE entries leave.

**F4 — finding (2), the react `ListView` element's `filterableFields` prop: confirmed; follow-up with objectui's reader removal.** `REACT_FIELD_SPECS.ListView.fields` (`validate-react-page-props.ts:773`) lists the prop as field-bearing and its test (`validate-react-page-props.test.ts:692-694`) authors it inside a JSX source string. A react page's `source` is parsed against no list-view schema, so the tombstone cannot reach it; objectui's reader at `origin/main` still honours it, so the prop works today and becomes a silent no-op once objectui's follow-up lands. The react-props lint should then refuse it by name rather than check its field references. Not this PR's surface; it belongs with the objectui follow-up.

**F5 — finding (3), the objectui follow-up sites: confirmed at `origin/main` `df943a2a1`.** `packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx:3464` forwards `viewDef.filterableFields ?? listSchema.filterableFields` (the PR's `:3448` has moved); `packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx:4654-4680` is the `filterFields` whitelist memo; `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx:3124` forwards it and `:1030` keeps it in a key list; `packages/plugin-view/src/index.tsx:90` registers the input; `packages/types/src/objectql.ts:2625` and `:2966` declare it locally; `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts:1300` reads `.shape.filterableFields` by reference, so the tombstone flows into the twin on the next pin bump while the member still exists and the pinned build keeps compiling; `packages/plugin-list/src/index.tsx:123` withholds it on a page `list-view` node. The seat files the objectui card when this lands, as the dispatch says.
